questions.stem: What happens to a sodium atom when it forms an ionic bond with chlorine?

options.text: It loses one proton to form Na⁺
It shares one electron with chlorine
It loses one electron to form Na⁺
It gains one electron to form Na⁻

questions.explanation: Sodium (Group 1) loses its one outer shell electron to form a Na⁺ ion. This gives it a full outer shell (the same electron configuration as neon).

questions.stem: When magnesium reacts with oxygen, what is the charge on the magnesium ion formed?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is in Group 2 and loses its two outer shell electrons to achieve a full outer shell, forming a Mg²⁺ ion.

questions.stem: Why does a chlorine atom form a Cl⁻ ion?

options.text: It loses one electron to get a full outer shell
It shares one electron with another atom
It gains one electron to get a full outer shell

questions.explanation: Chlorine is in Group 7 with 7 outer electrons. It needs to gain one more electron to achieve a full outer shell of 8, forming a Cl⁻ ion.

questions.stem: What type of structure do ionic compounds form?
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds form a giant ionic lattice, a regular arrangement of alternating positive and negative ions held together by strong electrostatic forces in all directions.

questions.stem: An atom has the electronic structure 2, 8, 2. What ion will it form?

options.text: It will not form an ion

questions.explanation: An atom with electronic structure 2, 8, 2 is in Group 2 (magnesium). It loses its 2 outer electrons to form a 2+ ion with the stable electron configuration 2, 8.

questions.stem: In the formation of sodium chloride, the total number of electrons is:

options.text: Doubled because each atom shares its electrons
Unchanged because electrons are only transferred, not created or destroyed

questions.explanation: During ionic bonding, electrons are transferred from one atom to another, but no electrons are created or destroyed. The total number of electrons remains the same.

questions.stem: Which pair of elements is most likely to form an ionic bond?
questions.explanation: Potassium is a metal (Group 1) and bromine is a non-metal (Group 7). Ionic bonds form between metals and non-metals, where electrons are transferred.
